paper.title: Causal Bandits with Unknown Graph Structure

settings.name_in_paper: Causal bandit with unknown causal graph (single-node interventions, single reward generating variable)
unmapped: Actions are the nK single-node interventions do(X_i=x) on n variables of an unknown causal DAG, each with domain [K]
Learner observes values of all variables in addition to the reward
Learner is given the essential graph and the observational distribution P(X), but not the causal graph
Learner knows the causal-effect identifiability constant eps_c (Assumption 2) and reward identifiability gap Delta_R (Assumption 3)
Causal sufficiency, Markov and faithfulness assumptions (Assumption 1)
settings.definition_quote: At every round $t$, the learner pulls $a_t = \text{do}(X_t = x_t)$ based on the knowledge from previous rounds and observes a random reward $R_t$ and the values of all $X\in\mathcal{X}$. The objective of the learner is to minimize the cumulative regret $R_T = T\mu_{a^*} - \sum_{t=1}^{T}\mu_{a_t}$ without knowing the causal graph $D$.

settings.name_in_paper: nK-arm Gaussian causal bandit class (lower bound)
unmapped: Actions are nK single-node interventions on n variables of an unknown causal graph; reward directly influenced by one variable
settings.definition_quote: For a bandit instance in $nK$-arm Gaussian causal bandit class, actions are composed by single-node interventions over $n$ variables ... with $|\mathcal{A}| = nK$. The reward for every action is Gaussian distributed and is directly influenced by one of $\mathcal{X}$.

algorithms.name: CN-UCB (Central Node UCB) for causal trees

bound.regime: T >> T_1 = K B (2+d) log_2 n

symbols.K_dom: domain size of each variable (number of values per intervention)
symbols.n_nodes: number of variables (nodes) in the causal graph
symbols.d_max: maximum degree of the skeleton of the causal tree

conditions: causal graph is a directed tree

source.label: thm:general_causal_tree
source.quote: Suppose we run CN-UCB with $T\gg T_1$ interventions in total and $T_2 := T-T_1$. Then with probability at least $1-\delta$, we have $R_T = \widetilde{O}\left(K\max\left\{\frac{1}{\Delta^2}, \frac{1}{\varepsilon^2}\right\}d(\log n)^2+\sqrt{KT}\right)$, where $d:=d_{\mathrm{max}}(\mathrm{skeleton}(D))$ and $\widetilde{O}$ ignores poly-log terms non-regarding to $n$.

results.notes: Regret defined through means (pseudo-regret) but bound holds w.p. 1-delta. Õ hides polylog terms not involving n (including log(1/delta), log T). Number of arms is n*K.

symbols.d_max: maximum degree of causal tree skeleton
symbols.B_samp: per-intervention sample count B = max{32/Delta_R^2 log(8nK/delta), 2/eps_c^2 log(8n^2K^2/delta)}

conditions: causal graph is a directed tree

source.label: lemma:general_causal_tree_sample
source.quote: Set $B = \max\{\frac{32}{\Delta^2}\log\left(\frac{8nK}{\delta}\right), \frac{2}{\varepsilon^2}\log\left(\frac{8n^2K^2}{\delta}\right)\}$, with probability at least $1-\delta$, stage 2 in Algorithm~\ref{algo:general_causal_tree} outputs the true key node within $KB(2+d)\log_2n+B$ interventions

results.notes: Number of interventions needed to identify the reward-generating node correctly with prob 1-delta.

symbols.d_max: max over chain components of the maximum degree
symbols.C_D: number of chain components of the essential graph

conditions: causal graph is a causal forest

source.label: thm:forest
source.quote: Then under Assumptions~\ref{assump:causal},~\ref{assump:bdd} and~\ref{assump:reward_gap}, with probability at least $1-\delta$, we have $R_T = \widetilde{O}\left(K\max\left\{\frac{1}{\Delta^2}, \frac{1}{\varepsilon^2}\right\}(d+C(D))(\log n)^2+\sqrt{KT}\right)$

results.notes: Õ ignores polylog terms not involving n.

bound.regime: T >> T_1 = B + KB log_2 n (omega(G_R) + d omega(G_R) + sum_G omega(G))

symbols.d_JT: maximum degree of the junction tree of the chain component G_R containing X_R
symbols.omega_R: clique number of chain component G_R
symbols.sum_omega: sum of clique numbers over all chain components of the essential graph
symbols.C_max: maximum number of maximal cliques over chain components

conditions: clique graph of every chain component is intersection-incomparable

source.label: thm:lower_bdd
source.quote: Let $\mathcal{E}$ be the set of $nK$-armed Gaussian bandits ... where the instances in $\mathcal{E}$ does not satisfy Assumption~\ref{assump:bdd}. We show that the minimax regret is $\inf_{\pi\in\Pi}\sup_{\nu\in\mathcal{E}} \mathbb{E}[R_T(\pi,\nu)] = \Omega(\sqrt{nKT})$

conditions: instances satisfy Assumption 2 but not Assumption 3 (reward identifiability)

source.label: thm:lower_reward_gap
source.quote: Let $\mathcal{E}$ be the set of $nK$-armed Gaussian bandits ... where the instances in $\mathcal{E}$ satisfy Assumption~\ref{assump:bdd} but does not satisfy Assumption~\ref{assump:reward_gap}. We show that the minimax regret is $\inf_{\pi\in\Pi}\sup_{\nu\in\mathcal{E}} \mathbb{E}[R_T(\pi,\nu)] = \Omega(\sqrt{nKT})$
